label: echoed r as first copy-phase input (recall_idx 1), long sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, almost exclusively when the input token is r (99.9% of mass). 95% of mass is at recall_idx 1, i.e. the step right after <DEL> where the first original token r is fed back in (first_tok = r, prev_tok = <DEL>); the remaining ~5% is at recall_idx 2 when r is fed back one step later. Magnitude grows with sequence length / outputs remaining: near zero for L <= 5, weak at L = 6, strongest at L = 8-9 (most activations at t = 8-10). Top activations (~0.8-1.0 of max) occur when the sequence starts r r, giving a second weaker activation on the next r. Does not fire in the original or delimiter phases, nor on r inputs in later copy positions (recall_idx >= 3), nor on other tokens. The predicate requiring L >= 7 trades recall on weak short-sequence activations for precision; without the L condition, recall is 0.88 (mass 0.95) but precision only 0.39 because many L = 4-6 cases are silent.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: r, f, z, -, k, o; least: 2, x, g, 0) and the token being output (most: r, k, h, o, 0, d; least: u, q, -, v); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=1, L=9 & t=10, L=8 & t=9.
